summary: Added 5 knowledge API methods to the API return object in gui/public/api-client.js: getKnowledge, updateKnowledge, deleteKnowledge, promoteKnowledge, moveKnowledge.
getKnowledge uses buildQueryString to construct the query from a params object.
updateKnowledge merges scope and project_slug (undefined when falsy) into the JSON body alongside the caller-supplied data object.
deleteKnowledge and promoteKnowledge pass scope/project_slug as URL query parameters via buildQueryString.
moveKnowledge sends source_scope, source_project_slug (undefined when falsy), and project_slug in the JSON body.
All 5 methods encode the id path segment via encodeURIComponent.
Added 20 new tests to tests/gui/api-client.test.ts covering URL construction, body shape, query-string omission of falsy values, and encodeURIComponent encoding for each method.
Full test suite: 85 files / 2537 tests — all passing, zero regressions.

comments.note: api-client.js uses ES5-style var declarations and function expressions throughout, while the rest of the project uses modern ES modules (const/let/arrow functions). This is intentional for browser compatibility in the SPA but could be modernised to ES module syntax if a bundler is ever introduced. No action needed under the current architecture.

The falsy-to-undefined coercion pattern `projectSlug || undefined` is used consistently across updateKnowledge, deleteKnowledge, promoteKnowledge, and moveKnowledge. This is correct but slightly fragile — a slug of '0' would be dropped. In practice project slugs are always non-empty strings, so this is safe; documenting for awareness.

No existing tests covered the knowledge section of the API client prior to this WP. The 20 new tests in api-client.test.ts now cover URL construction, body shape, query-param omission, and encodeURIComponent encoding for all 5 methods.

AC-by-AC verification: (1) All 5 methods present in the API return object using the request() helper pattern ✓; (2) getKnowledge delegates to buildQueryString — omits undefined/empty params, encodes special chars ✓; (3) updateKnowledge merges scope and project_slug into body via Object.assign — project_slug coerced to undefined when falsy ✓; (4) deleteKnowledge and promoteKnowledge pass scope/project_slug as URL query params via buildQueryString ✓; (5) moveKnowledge sends source_scope, source_project_slug (undefined when falsy), and project_slug in JSON body ✓; (6) All 5 methods encode the id path segment via encodeURIComponent ✓.

Edge-case review: getKnowledge(null) returns bare /api/knowledge (buildQueryString early-returns ''); promoteKnowledge sends no body (no Content-Type header); updateKnowledge merge order gives scope/project_slug precedence over caller-supplied data — correct by design; moveKnowledge '' sourceProjectSlug correctly drops to undefined in JSON serialisation.

comments.note: updateKnowledge uses Object.assign({}, data, { scope, project_slug }) — the merge order means scope/project_slug always override same-named keys in data. This is correct and intentional, but worth noting for future maintainers: callers cannot override scope via the data argument.
promoteKnowledge correctly sends no body (request() receives only 2 args). The 'does not send a request body' test (line 363) explicitly verifies opts.body is undefined — good defensive coverage.

No code-quality issues found. All 5 methods are consistent in style and correctly follow the established buildQueryString / encodeURIComponent / request() pattern used by all other API client methods.

In moveKnowledge, sourceProjectSlug uses the || undefined coercion (consistent with updateKnowledge/deleteKnowledge/promoteKnowledge), but targetProjectSlug does NOT. This asymmetry is intentional — a move always requires a target — but a brief inline comment like '// target is always required' would help future maintainers understand it is not an oversight.

[documentation-forward] The new knowledge section in api-client.js has no JSDoc comments on any of its 5 methods. The existing methods in the file also lack per-method docs, but the knowledge group is the first to introduce non-obvious semantics (scope/project_slug coercion, Object.assign merge order, promoteKnowledge sending no body). Adding brief JSDoc to these 5 methods — documenting parameters, the falsy-to-undefined coercion rule, and the merge precedence in updateKnowledge — would significantly aid future contributors.

The Object.assign merge order in updateKnowledge ({}, data, { scope, project_slug }) correctly gives scope/project_slug precedence over caller-supplied data keys. This is the right design, but a caller passing scope or project_slug inside data will have them silently overridden. The QA pipeline already noted this; it is correct by design and requires no change.
